title: spawn_palette
description: The `spawn_palette` content kind (megaplan 1.7 and task 8-A1): one entry of the Overlord's spawn palette (and of the Server Heat squads, which name entries of this kind). One entry per file; an entry is one spawn action: `count` figures (1 to 8, the `n` of the `spawn` message) at one spot, for `cost` Threat Points, so a bigger spawn is a dearer entry. `group` files the entry under a tab of the palette (gang, law, machine, monster). `hostile` is true when the spawned figures attack players. `kind` is `minecraft` (a vanilla mob, `mob` is its entity id) or `night_city` (a figure of the host's own game, spawned through the `spawn` message of Phase 0 (d): `rec` is its class, `faction` the attitude group it joins). A Night City entry also has `squad`, the Minecraft squad that stands in for it when it cannot be spawned there: for a Minecraft-only player, for a host whose `spawns` toggle is off, or when the Phase 0 (d) spawn does not work (the written fallback). `rec` is one of the classes of the megaplan 1.9 `spawn` row: ganger, ncpd, maxtac and drone (turrets cannot be spawned in the host's game, Phase 0 (d): a turret entry is a `minecraft` entry). `faction` is a game attitude group name (tygerClaws, maelstrom, valentinos, 6thStreet, animals, voodooBoys, scavenger, wraiths, kurtz_army, police, arasaka). The wire carries only the class and the faction, so the NCPD patrol and the enforcers are the same Night City class (the enforcers are a dearer squad with a tougher Minecraft stand-in). `cooldown_s` is how long before the same entry can be spawned again. A `mob` (and a squad's `mob`) must work in the replica at any hour: the server's overworld zombifies piglins and hoglins and burns the daylight undead (minecraft:burn_in_daylight, except the fire-immune wither skeleton), so those are not used; a `hostile` one attacks players unprovoked in any light (no enderman or spider); and none explodes or breaks blocks (no creeper, ghast, breeze or blaze). A spawn is guest-caused: anything it does to a host (an explosion, a hit) names the Overlord player as its cause, so the host's guest toggles apply. Text is original. A file with the same id as a default replaces it.
